Everton XI: Travers; Patterson, Tarkowski, Keane, Mykolenko; Hackney, Deswbury-Hall, Armstrong, Ndiaye; George, Barry.

Here's how we start against Newcastle. UTT! 🔵📺 https://t.co/2VsWpyRq02 pic.twitter.com/vpnLPTRmLl.

Newcastle United manager ​Matthias Jaissle is ‌refusing to dwell on the departure of key players that has left his club in turmoil going into the new season, as they step up their preparations against Everton at Murrayfield this evening.

Jaissle was recruited from Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli after Eddie Howe left last month, with the German coach joining a club who have lost Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes in quick succession.

According to recent reports, “It’s a challenge, a big challenge, always when there’s a transitional period. ‌But it’s ‌not time to ⁠complain, it doesn’t make sense to see the negative things,” Jaissle mentioned.

“We want to see the chance in that situation and that’s our approach from day one. We are here to do our ⁠best job. We want to support the players, the current squad.

“There will be adjustments to see in the coming days, weeks. But for now it’s only focused on the daily work, the work we can influence. That’s all that ​matters now.”.

The 38-year-old coach arrived in Newcastle ‌having won two Austrian Bundesliga titles with Red Bull Salzburg before leading Al-Ahli to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.

He remained tight-lipped about newly introduced signings.

“Obviously, in that transition phase, the players who left the club were ‌great ​players, great characters, experienced ⁠players. This is now a vacuum,” he said.

“Either we adjust something in the squad, by signing these players, these profiles, or other players ⁠need to step up and fill ​these positions, these leadership roles. I’m quite optimistic, we can work in both scenarios.”.

Jaissle said he had a ​clear vision of how he wants his team to play.

Recent findings suggest that “The phrase how Newcastle ‌should play like is front-footed, intense, ​aggressive and of course also successful. ​In the end, it’s all about what ⁠I can ⁠say and it’s also why I’m sitting here,” he said.

“The approach we have as a coaching team and the identity of Newcastle is famed for, it’s so linked so close together - which is a perfect fit in my eyes and ​that’s going to be exciting.”.

“Because Kostoulas came back from the international break with a small issue,” said Hurzeler when asked why Georginio started ahead of Kostoulas.

“Therefore we had to make this decision, it wasn't a tactical decision, we had to take care of the health of the player.

”It's just a small issue, he came back from being with Greece, so something was there, but he didn't feel like 100 per cent.”.

Hull pounced at the death as Oli McBurnie struck twice in added time to snatch a 2-0 victory against high-flying Brighton at the MKM Stadium.

Hurzeler’s side were dominant but could not find a way through, thwarted on several occasions by Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis.

Industry observers note that hurzeler added: "For 65 minutes we indicated a good performance then we dropped our intensity, levels and standards. In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon a frustrating game but we have to keep going.

"We will analyse it. That's the process we follow. I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time.".

Brighton, for the first time this season, seemed to run out of gas in the closing stages and the the Costinha sending off tipped the balance in Hull’s favour.

In a recent development, hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role. We made a decision, at that moment, a wrong decision, but we will analyse it.

“My team was desperate to win it, of course, in certain elements be more patient, be more disciplined, be more structured.

“That's what we missed, not only in the last minutes, also in the minutes before, and again, we will analyse it and make it better.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rangers maintained their strong run of domestic form by defeating Motherwell 2-1 at Fir Park.

Emmanuel Fernandez had his headed opener for the away side cancelled out by a Jake Girdwood-Reich effort before Ryan Naderi’s deflected winner. It means Rangers are second and four points behind Premiership leaders Celtic with a game in hand while Motherwell sit 10th after their latest defeat.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Sources indicate that I was at the game played in bitterly cold North Lanarkshire conditions. Here are some of the things I spotted.

Whisper it in hushed tones... but this is the type of game that teams who go on to clinch silverware usually grind out. The expected goals tally of both sides show the tale of the tape, where not too dissimilar to Rangers’ 1-0 at Ibrox last time out, Derek McInnes’ side battered on the door without getting through.

Industry observers note that motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen was doing his best ‘you shall not pass’ Gandalf impression, but much like The Balrog dragging the grey wizard from Lord of the Rings into the abyss, eventually his resistance was broken. It was messy but Rangers cared not as they got their winner just before a minimal amount of stoppage time was added on. It’s a clash teams of the recent past in Govan coughed points up in and making it 13 unbeaten domestically will be of great satisfaction to boss McInnes.

According to recent reports, motherwell under Alfred Johansson have set their stall out as a side who want to dominate the ball but that hasn’t happened in either home game against Rangers or Celtic. Both sides of the Old Firm have come to Fir Park and been able to dictate play, Martin O’Neill’s side winning 2-0 last month, having controlled proceedings with well over 60% possession. This was much the same albeit the Fir Park defence stood valiantly until they were eventually overwhelmed, Rangers enjoying just under that 60% mark in terms of time on the ball.

It has been revealed that motherwell fans, and supporters of other provincial clubs, have been used to these types of games against Glasgow’s big two over the years. It’s a defensive stand that more often than not ends in defeat, but it’s more of a shock to the system for Motherwell, given what they have built over the last 18 months. Rangers’ winner was perhaps harsh with the effort put in but the amount of chances coughed up proved there could be little complaints over their visitors claiming all three points. Key playmaker Ibrahim Stated looked visibly emotional after being subbed in the first half with injury and that will be of major concern to boss Johansson, with much of his side’s good attacking play usually involving the Nigerian.

Since replacing an injured Lawrence Shankland last time out versus Motherwell, Ryan Naderi has been a man transformed. He bundled home the winner off defender Martin Moormann here to make it 11 goal contributions in as many games. Questions over quality were abundant last term upon his arrival from Hansa Rostock but he has been vital for McInnes this term.

Amid long-term blows to Shankland and Youssef Chermiti, Naderi has firmly made himself Rangers’ main man in attack. Any striker coming into the team would need to play alongside him as it’s hard to see how they function without him. It might be unconventional at times but Naderi’s pressing and knack of being in the right place at the right time is proving invaluable.

This clash between Motherwell and Rangers was the first time since Opta records began in season 2005/06 that there was not one Scottish player in the starting line-up of a top-flight match. As conversations continue over development of young talent in our country, it’s perhaps inevitable it became a talking point across analysis of the match.

In a recent development, let’s get off our high horses for a minute though as the conversation with this particular game needs more nuance. Alex Lowry and Stephen O’Donnell are regular starters for Motherwell but both were unavailable, while club captain Paul McGinn is only recently back from long-term injury. James Penrice would likely have been a starter for Rangers had he been fully fit while Findlay Curtis did get on to make a key impact in the winner. Callum Hendry offered more bite to the home attack at the other end. All of that is not to say a lack of development Scottish talent isn’t an concern, it is, but perhaps this stat isn’t the platform to build that argument from.

Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031 - with goalkeeper David Raya set to join him in committing his future to the club.

The England midfielder is expected to sign the latest contract soon, which is set to put him alongside Bukayo Saka as Arsenal's top earner. Saka is on a deal worth over £350,000 a week.

It has been revealed that and Raya, 31, is understood to have agreed a deal in principle to extend his terms. Both players' existing deals expire in 2028.

Rice joined Arsenal in 2023 for £105million from West Ham and has established himself as the fulcrum of their midfield, helping steer them to the Premier League title last season.

The 27-year-old played 55 games in all competitions last season as the Gunners reached their first Champions League final since 2006, but lost out to Paris Saint-Germain.

His contract talks have been ongoing from at least March and are now finalised.

Raya joined Arsenal from Brentford on loan in the same summer, and signed a permanent deal a year later.

Declan Rice has agreed a upcoming-five year deal at Arsenal that will run until the summer of 2031.

David Raya has agreed a deal in principle to stay on, with his current deal expiring in 2028.

Rice had confirmed a latest deal was close over the weekend when speaking on international duty with England.

'I've been extremely lucky that I've managed to play at such a consistent level throughout my career.

'I've always been stable in the clubs I've been at.

'A fresh contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

'I'm extremely lucky that I'm at a club like Arsenal, where my manager [Mikel Arteta] and my team-mates put so much energy in me.

'I'm extremely lucky I don't have to think about that stuff.'.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was a second league win in a row after a shaky spell of results and left Danny Hollands’ men third in the table and just three points behind leaders Egham.

Early on Hayes’ Ben Shroll put a low ball into the area but Kaylen Hinds shot over from the edge of the box.

Roberts put Bognor in the lead as his run down the left saw him beat his marker before coolly sliding it under Rhys Forster in the Hayes goal on eight minutes.

Amari Fashanu won a corner for the visitors with his low strike but Benny Read headed it out. Liam Ferdinand created an opening but missed his chace in front of goal.

Industry observers note that for the Rocks, Henry Nevill hooked a cross in from the left but Callum Laycock looped it up into the air with his head. Lennie Smith sped down the right but his cross-shot was saved.

Bognor extended their lead on 25 minutes when Roberts' shot was pushed out only as far as McDonald, who diverted it into the net on the rebound, despite Forster getting something on it.

From McDonald's corner, Tommy Block was denied in a crowded penalty area. On 38 minutes Joshua Edwards had to receive treatment as he took a bash to the head in a challenge with Laycock.

Smith got on the breakaway for Bognor and he fed McDonald, who struck a shot wide along the deck. Harry Grant blasted over as Hayes were very wasteful in front of goal.

Four minutes after the break, a fierce ball in from Dernell Wynter saw Ferdinand divert it in from close range to make it 2-1.

It has been revealed that shroll got another dangerous ball into the box but Amos Nasha's header was directed straight at Tommy Scott. Shroll went into the book for a shoulder barge into the back of Smith. Kaya Tshaka's free-kick picked out Block but his header was saved.

Sources indicate that tshaka swiped at a chance of his own and he had to come off injured. Ethan Robb replaced him.

It has been revealed that nevill blazed a cross from the left too high before Fashanu hit a curling effort with his right foot and Scott palmed it out. Fashanu hit a corner deep towards the back post with Shroll under it, but Laycock and Scott combined to keep it out.

Recent findings suggest that nasha did well to pass the ball to Ferdinand and he hit the right post with his low effort on 69 minutes. Roberts was replaced by Ben Anderson for the Rocks and Nasha went into the book as he pulled Nevill back.

It has been revealed that scott pulled out a wonderful save down to his right to keep Grant’s low volleyed effort from just outside the area. Ferdinand was offside on the rebound.

Ollie Lovell came off on 80 minutes for Bognor, then the referee pulled up injured with a strained calf so Bognor's public address announcer, Peter Kelly-Sullivan, had to take up the flag for linesman’s duty for the remainder of the game.

Brendan Matthew had a header diverted wide when he had the goal at his mercy in the 94th minute.

It was a nervy final moments for the Rocks with the visitors always a danger but they held on for the win.

Next up is the highly-anticipated game away to Jersey Bulls – and over 200 Bognor fans are expected to make the trip to the island on Saturday.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there was no disguising the satisfaction in Tuur Rommens' voice as he reflected on Rangers' late 2-1 victory over Motherwell. It provided the Belgian defender with further evidence of a team learning learning how to grind out results and develop a winning mentality to overcome hurdles when it matters most.

Sources indicate that rangers looked in danger of leaving Fir Park frustrated on Saturday night after a performance in which their attacking intent was not always matched by clinical finishing. Motherwell goalkeeper Alex Paulsen had done everything within his power to earn his side a point, producing a string of outstanding saves, but Rangers refused to settle for a draw.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Their persistence was eventually rewarded in the 88th minute when Ryan Naderi’s effort took a deflection off Martin Moorman, wrong-footing Paulsen and finding the net. Those heroics sparked jubilant celebrations among the sizeable travelling support.

Rommens acknowledged that such a dramatic conclusion in North Lanarkshire could provide a significant boost to morale inside the away dressing room, praising his team-mates' willingness to keep pushing despite facing a goalkeeper in inspired form.

“The spirit was good and especially when you score a goal in the last minute of the game, it always gives an extra boost,” said the left-back. “Everybody was very happy in the dressing room. It's never easy to come here and to win. Last year we didn't win here, so it's nice to come here and win and get the three points.

Industry observers note that “We had a lot of chances. The finish was not always there, but we played a very good game. It feels like we've gained these two points. Their goalkeeper did an amazing job. It's not only our finishing, it's also credit that he saves a lot of shots. Of course, if it stays 1-1, you're thinking, ‘oh, come on, we need to get another one’. But at the end, we got what we deserved.”.

Rangers were left to rue too many dropped points last season, and Rommens is acutely aware of how big the difference between settling for a point and claiming all three can be over the course of a campaign.

The connection between the players and supporters is another factor the 23-year-old believes is proving invaluable in helping Rangers navigate difficult moments.

Recent findings suggest that “The fanbase is unbelievable. It doesn't feel like an away game because there are so many fans with us,” he added. “When you score you feel a lot of emotions. You feel that they're so happy, we're so happy, so it gives us an extra boost to go again on Tuesday and try to get another win.”.

Attention now turns to Rangers’ game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday night, with Derek McInnes’ side looking to capitalise on a run of three successive home fixtures and build on their 13-game unbeaten streak.

The bigger picture remains firmly in their sights, although Rommens is not interested in becoming distracted by the current state of the title race.

“It's been a long time (since we last played at Ibrox). So it will be nice to play in front of our fans again,” he stated. “I think at home we have to maintain our good run. You just need to keep winning and at the end you'll see where you're at. But if you keep winning, you'll be up there.”.

Since Bexhill secured a win in the reverse fixture in September, Midhurst have struggled to recover from internal strife that saw their manager and a number of players depart, with a run of poor results that has plunged them into the relegation mire.

Meanwhile, Bexhill have managed to strike a rich vein of form with a squad that blends youth with experience and a strong sense of togetherness and solidarity.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Missing Luke Donaldson with a three-match ban, Pirates gaffer Jay Skinner-Swain kept Ash Latuske and Ryan Moir in their attacking positions on the flanks with Charlie Scarles slotting into an advanced role in midfield.

Bexhill couldn’t have hoped for a better start. In the first minute Theo Coombs had a chance well saved but from the resulting corner Charlie Playford ghosted into the six yard box to beat all-comers with a bullet header from point blank range.

Three minutes later Latuske beat two men with a powerful run down the right to set up Shonk and the Bexhill record goalscorer made no mistake in adding another to his tally.

It has been revealed that it looked like Bexhill would run amok but it’s all credit to the young Midhurst lads that they didn’t just fold. They put in some decent enough approach moves but the Pirates defence had the measure of them.

Industry observers note that at the other end, another goal looked almost inevitable. On 25 minutes Shonk had an effort cleared off the line from a Moir corner. Shortly after, Scarles had an effort well saved by the young Midhurst keeper who was keeping his side in with a sniff.

Just before the break there was nothing he could do though as Latuske lashed in a drive that had the keeper beaten all ends up but the ball somehow bounced back out into play off the inside of the post.

Bexhill went in two goals to the good at half-time but on the balance of play and chances it should have been more.

Almost inevitably Midhurst delivered a scare early in the second half. Just five minutes in, a runner skipped past the Bexhill defensive lines and delivered a ball which was swept into the Pirates net. It was followed minutes later by a good effort that required a fine save from Finn Holter.

According to recent reports, but the moment soon passed for Midhurst and Bexhill got back in amongst it. The killer goal came on 55 and it was that man Coombs again, benefitting from some more great play from Latuske and swivelling to tuck the chance away.

In a recent development, now it really was all Bexhill as Midhurst wilted under the pressure. On 65 minutes Latuske was at it again, this time setting up Shonk, whose shot curled just wide of the post. It was the briefest of respites for Midhurst as Moir played in Coombs on the left and this time he turned provider, chipping in a perfect cross for Shonk to nod home for 4-1.

Sources indicate that bexhill were rampant now and on 76 minutes substitute Jack Samways wrapped it up at 5-1 to the Pirates with the pick of the afternoon’s goals. Winning the ball just inside the box he crashed a perfect half volley into the Brockley Road End net.

It was no less than Bexhill deserved for a thoroughly professional demolition job on their hapless visitors.

The Pirates move up sixth in the league and have a chance to keep their current run going with the long trip over to Pagham on Saturday afternoon.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 19:30, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 20:07.
  • Arsenal spurned the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League table as they were forced to come from behind to draw 2-2 with Newcastle United at St James' Park.
  • Warned to expect a "hellish" fixture at a ground where they have not had much luck in recent years, the champions were in the ascendancy from the off and deservedly went into half time ahead courtesy of Eberechi Eze's first-time finish.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 19:30, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 20:07.

Arsenal spurned the chance to go eight points clear at the top of the Premier League table as they were forced to come from behind to draw 2-2 with Newcastle United at St James' Park.

Warned to expect a "hellish" fixture at a ground where they have not had much luck in recent years, the champions were in the ascendancy from the off and deservedly went into half time ahead courtesy of Eberechi Eze's first-time finish.

Matthias Jaissle's men were booed off at half time after generating just 0.08 Expected Goals during the opening period, but that number shot up just four minutes into the second half, when a gift from Martin Odegaard handed Harvey Barnes an equaliser against the run of play.

Barnes's strike triggered a magnificent Newcastle response, one that saw them rewarded with the game's third goal through Malick Thiaw just past the hour mark following a corner scramble.

However, the momentum pendulum swung back Arsenal's way shortly after, as the effervescent Noni Madueke drew the holders level to set up a grand-stand finish.

Nine minutes of added time was not enough for either team to snatch a winner, as Arsenal extended their lead over Manchester City and Brighton & Hove Albion to six points, while Newcastle remain 12th with 13 points.

For all of Arsenal's first-half dominance, the Gunners were guilty of a perpetual shortcoming in the Arteta era; not putting the game to bed before the break.

Staunch Newcastle defending and shoddy Arsenal finishing denied the visitors a healthier first-half advantage, and while the champions cut complacent figures at the start of the second half, Jaissle's half-time team talk worked a treat.

Odegaard's blunder helped the hosts on their way, and Arsenal found themselves unfamiliarly rattled for a good 30 minutes, until the increasingly impressive Madueke came to the fore again.

However, the winger himself admitted that his side should have been at least three to the good at half time, yet more evidence that a killer finisher is a matter of priority for the January transfer window.

"Absolutely clinical!" Eberechi Eze scores his first Premier League goal of the season to give Arsenal the lead ? https://t.co/34IbZuuJuN.

Seven months after his last Premier League goal - against the Magpies - the Englishman does it again, rifling in a slick side-footed strike from 12 yards after Kai Havertz's delightful through ball.

Havertz had robbed Lewis Hall of possession before slipping in Eze, who left Lukas Hornicek rooted to the spot.

Recent findings suggest that "Horrendous error!" Harvey Barnes puts Newcastle level ? https://t.co/YWrHZPxBIo.

A howler from Odegaard, a flicker of hope for Newcastle!

The Arsenal captain tries to volley a throw-in close to his own penalty area, but gets his connection all wrong and slices the ball into William Osula's path.

The Newcastle striker spots Barnes in acres of space in the left of the box, and the latter takes one touch to set himself before calmly slotting home into the bottom corner!

Sources indicate that malick Thiaw is in the right place to fire it in and give Newcastle the lead against Arsenal! ? https://t.co/nthaH3aOJD.

When we talk about a game of two halves, this is exactly what we mean.

Dan Burn finds himself all alone as a corner is floated in; replays show that Jurrien Timber - his marker - was being held back by Osula as he tried to catch up to him.

The towering Newcastle defender heads the ball back into the danger area, and after an almighty scramble, Thiaw pokes home from a yard out!

Recent findings suggest that noni Madueke equalises for Arsenal! ? https://t.co/VNXOoNDxiJ.

Champions respond how champions respond.

Odegaard just broke down a counter-attack by picking the wrong pass, but the Arsenal captain gets it right this time, laying off Madueke on the right-hand side.

The winger cuts inside, works a yard for a shot from inside the D, and the ball finds its way into the bottom corner via Hornicek's gloves.

The Newcastle goalkeeper ought to have done better, but credit the free-flowing move from the visitors, who are level again!

Sources indicate that "I reckon 2-2 was a fair result." Noni Madueke reflects on Arsenal's performance against Newcastle at St James' Park ? https://t.co/UfDi5SGgat.

Both frustrating and fascinating to watch for Arsenal fans, Madueke once again proved a capable deputy for Bukayo Saka on the right.

The England international had six shots in total, made one key pass and registered four successful dribbles, albeit while missing two major chances that could, or should, have been the difference between Arsenal taking home either one or three points.

Possession: Newcastle 34%-66% Arsenal.

Shots on target: Newcastle 3-4 Arsenal.

Arsenal resume their Champions League campaign at home to Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday evening, before the significant one against Manchester City in next Sunday's Premier League showdown.

Meanwhile, Newcastle have over a week to recuperate before they travel to Arsenal's closest Premier League title challengers Brighton & Hove Albion next Sunday.

Brian Madjo, 17, electrifies Villa despite Super Cup defeat by PSG

📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4852 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.
  • Sources indicate that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo.
  • Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unai Emery’s Aston Villa 2.0 remain under construction but from the wreckage of a difficult summer there has emerged a potential star for the future.

Sources indicate that emery may have now suffered four successive defeats in the Super Cup, yet the big positive from a balmy night in Salzburg was the performance of teenage forward Brian Madjo. Aged 17 years and 212 days, Madjo became the youngest player to start and score in this continental showpiece, just over a week after he was given permission to play for his club.

Signed from Metz for £10m in January, Madjo had been prevented from playing because of Fifa’s rules on the international transfer of minors. Villa’s appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport to have him registered was upheld on August 4 and what a prospect he appears.

Born in Enfield but raised in Luxembourg, there has been a huge buzz around him since his arrival in the new year.

Paris St-Germain have produced an abundance of talented teenagers over the years and Madjo did not look out of place here.Désiré Doué’s second-half strike secured PSG the Super Cup – contested by the winners of the Champions League and Europa League – for the second successive year, but Emery will have seen enough to give him renewed confidence.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

His team played with all the resilience and bravery that has become a trademark, epitomised by the powerful Madjo and another teenager in midfielder George Hemmings.

Emery stated: “Brian has scored goals for us in pre-season and has shown his capacity to work in our idea. I am so happy because the young players were involved in our work and not playing last season.

In a recent development, “Of course there is still work to do but they showed they can play with us. They have responded fantastically and will then feel the confidence. With a loss you can never be happy but overall I am proud of all the players and everything we’ve done. Some changes will be needed but we’re confident.”.

This was a fine Villa performance to silence the doom merchants who have been fearing a troubled season. After the painful sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, Villa are clearly a team in transition. They are operating under restrictions to comply with Uefa’s financial rules and there is still the possibility of another important player leaving before the transfer deadline day.

England centre-back Ezri Konsa remains a priority target for Premier League champions Arsenal, and was absent here. Konsa, Emiliano Martínez and Ollie Watkins were all granted extended leave after their participation in the World Cup, which has done little to ease the fears of supporters over more departures. The trio will return to training this weekend.

Sources indicate that while some outsiders are predicting a difficult season for Villa, do not bother telling Emery. He has turned putting noses out of joint into an art form since sweeping into Villa Park and with him around anything feels possible.

The Basque remains optimistic about the future and those hopes will only have been underlined by the performance of Madjo. He bullied PSG centre-back Willian Pacho for much of the evening and even managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s magician Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.

Sources indicate that hemmings, 19, has emerged from the academy and already made a real impression on his manager. Despite the high regard for those youngsters, this always appeared likely to be a tough proposition against a full-strength PSG team. Indeed, before this game in Salzburg only 39 per cent of Europa League winners have beaten their Champions League rivals in this fixture.

The French champions did start slowly, but had been cranking up the pressure before taking a 20th minute lead with a spectacular strike from their Georgian superstar.

Doué forced a save from Marco Bizot and, after Villa failed to clear, the loose ball landed in the path of Kvaratskhelia, who cut inside on the left to his right foot before smashing a shot into the roof of the net.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

It was a strike of sheer power and accuracy, catching Bizot by surprise. PSG briefly appeared in control, but Villa responded superbly. In 17 minutes they created six goal-scoring chances before the outstanding Madjo finally made one of them count.

Before his goal, he had narrowly missed the target twice with a pair of headers from John McGinn’s crosses. Villa also had another opportunity 10 minutes before half-time, when Pacho’s mistake allowed Hemmings to run from the centre circle unopposed. As he entered the penalty area, the PSG defenders had raced back to recover and a promising moment ended with Madjo curling a shot wide.

Brian Madjo with a big chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

PSG goalkeeper Matvey Safonov then produced his first save just before the break, turning away Boubacar Kamara’s close-range header. Villa did carve out another golden chance when Madjo’s strength took hm past Pacho, but he hit the outside of the post. Madjo’s moment did come, though, as he once again bullied Pacho to divert a McGinn cross into the roof of the net.

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Industry observers note that villa were buoyant, but it was PSG who scored the crucial second goal after Doué was awarded the goal following a VAR review. Doué was sent clear down the right by substitute Ousmane Dembélé and confidently beat Bizot, with reviews concluding that he had been played onside by Matty Cash.

The game was refereed by Omar Artan, the Somali referee who was supposed to officiate at the World Cup but was denied entry to the United States.

Recent findings suggest that it became rather fractious as time began to tick away, with McGinn booked after complaining over the placement of a free-kick. Madjo was replaced by Tammy Abraham with 17 minutes left and this will be an evening he will never forget.

PSG (4-3-3): Safonov, Hakimi, Marquinhos, Pacho, Mendes (Hernandez 75), Neves (Ruiz 75), Vitinha, Emery, Akliouche, (Dembele 45), Doue (Mayulu 87), Kvaratskhelia (Buraldo 88).Substitutes: Chevalier (g), Zabarnyi, Digne, Fernandez, Barcola, Ndjantou, Mbaye.Villa (4-2-3-1): Bizot, Cash, Lindelof, Torres (Mings 80), Maatsen, Kamara (Bogarde 72), Gomes (Barkley 79), McGinn 7 (Alysson 73), Buendia, Hemmings, Madjo (Abraham 72).Substitutes: Wright (g), Asemota (g), Barkley, Nedeljkovic, Cisse, Rowe, Burrowes, Lynch.Booked: Gomes, Torres, McGinn.Referee: Omar Artan (Somalia).

In a recent development, after the officials and the Aston Villa players receive their medals, it is time for the 2026 Uefa Super Cup winners PSG to receive their medals. The last man up is their captain Marquinhos, who has won a staggering 40 trophies during his time at PSG. He takes the trophy from Uefa President Aleksander Ceferin and lifts it above his head alongside his teammates.

PSG are your 2026 UEFA Super Cup Champions 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/1qCKEQ0IPK.

Both Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have been heavily linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and neither player came off the bench for PSG tonight. Does that indicate that potentially those moves could be close, with neither played risked of picking up an injury?

Sources indicate that luis Enrique has now won 13 trophies with PSG. Serial winner 🏆 pic.twitter.com/RAsyI1Ui2s.

It has been revealed that 💬 "We are ALWAYS hungry you know... we want more, we want more" Désiré Doué reflects on PSG's UEFA Super Cup Final win.📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nwreU1Skz7.

Aston Villa will take on Borussia Mönchengladbach on Saturday in their final game of pre-season before they take on Brighton on the south coast on the opening weekend of the fresh Premier League season.

PSG play Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before they kick off the defence of their Ligue 1 crown at home against Rennes.

Possession: PSG 61%- Aston Villa 39%Shots: 12-15Shots on target: 6-4Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 29-34.

Buendia has a late chance to equalise for Aston Villa from Maatsen’s cross but his header goes wide.

Not long after, the final whistle goes and PSG win the Super Cup for the second straight year. Last year they beat Tottenham on penalties, this time they beat Aston Villa 2-1. Unai Emery’s side acquitted themselves well and will regret some of their missed chances tonight. An entertaining affair in Salzburg.

PSG win back-to-back UEFA Super Cup's following goals from Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue 🏆📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vzMx6rGjuo.

Dembele feeds a pass into the Villa box looking to pick out the run of Hakimi but there is slightly too much on it and Bizot is out to gather.

Into the final minute of added time we go.

Aston Villa are running out of time to find a late equaliser.

There will be five added minutes.

Maatsen brings Dembele down not far outside the Aston Villa box but play goes on as the latter gets up and shoots, with his effort saved by Bizot.

One final change for PSG as their other goalscorer tonight, Kvaratskhelia, is replaced by Beraldo. A defender comes on for an attacker as Luis Enrique’s side look to hold on for the victory.

Mayulu is coming on for Doue, whose goal may well have won back-to-back Super Cups for PSG.

The ball falls to Kvaratskhelia on the right side of the box and the Georgian chips it over Bizot but Cash is on hand to clear. Aston Villa then counter and Abraham feeds a pass forward at the perfect time to pick out the run of Alysson into the PSG box. Alysson then plays it across the six-yard box but neither Abraham nor Maatsen are there to meet the cross.

Double change for Aston Villa as Barkley and Mings replace Gomes and Torres, who were both on yellow cards.

It has been revealed that alysson, only just on the pitch, does brilliantly down Aston Villa’s right and drives into the PSG penalty area. His cross is parried away by Safonov straight into the path of Gomes, whose shot is blocked by Zaire-Emery.

Sources indicate that PSG are making a double substitution as Ruiz and L Hernandez come on. Neves and Mendes, who had been struggling with cramp, go off.

Aston Villa are going to make a triple change as Abraham, Alysson and Bogarde come on. 17-year-old Madjo is one of those to be replaced as is McGinn, who has been booked as he goes off. The Aston Villa captain is distinctly unimpressed with the officials.

In a recent development, the space opens up for Mendes to take on the shot from range and he obliges, forcing Bizot into a decent save. Kvaratskhelia is unable to make contact with the follow-up. Mendes seems to be struggling with some cramp.

We are nearly 70 minutes into the game but Unai Emery has still not turned to his bench yet.

In a recent development, aston Villa have an immediate chance to equalise through Hemmings but the 19-year-old’s effort from inside the box is straight at Safonov. That was a significant chance for Hemmings.

Down the other end, Gomes is booked for a challenge from behind on Doue.

The VAR has checked it and there was no offside so the original decision is overturned and the goal is given. Doue is played in behind by Dembele down the right channel and is played onside by Cash on the far side. Doue takes it into the Villa penalty area and gets it onto his left foot. He curls it past Bizot and into the far corner.

Desire Doue puts PSG 2-1 ahead despite originally being flagged offside 🫣📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/vnMIZCWJaj.

Sources indicate that doue has the ball in the Aston Villa net but the offside flag has gone up. However, has Cash played Doue onside?

Cash’s cross from the right picks out Buendia at the front post but the latter’s header is off target. Unai Emery will be pretty happy with his side’s performance through the hour mark.

Mendes is a touch fortunate not to be penalised for a foul on McGinn as the Aston Villa captain spun the Portuguese defender on halfway. The referee must have thought both players had a hold of each other but I would lean towards Mendes probably fouling McGinn.

Industry observers note that other than 10/15 minutes in and around Kvaratskhelia’s goal, Aston Villa have put in a good performance and have created more chances than PSG. If anything, it will be Villa who will be disappointed that they have not scored more than once.

Just inside the PSG penalty area, McGinn cuts onto his left to get his shot away and his deflected effort is saved by Safonov diving to his right.

One of Aston Villa’s coaches has been booked for some protestations after Torres is penalised for a foul on Doue. Torres is also booked for that challenge.

It has been revealed that two of Aston Villa’s best players tonight thus far have been teenagers; 19-year-old Hemmings and 17-year-old Madjo. Aston Villa have seen some key, senior players depart this summer but will take joy from the performances of this pair.

Luis Enrique has decided he needed to make a change at the break as Dembele replaces Akliouche, who was quiet on his official debut for PSG after his move from Monaco.

We are back under way in Salzburg.

Brian Madjo - remember the name.

Incredible to think he is only 17 years and 212 days old. He’s been all over PSG centre-back Willian Pacho and thoroughly deserves his goal.

Industry observers note that the teenager could even have had a hat-trick. What a second-half this could be.

Madjo has managed to steal the limelight from PSG’s Georgian magician Kvicha Kvaratskhelia, which is quite some achievement.

Possession: PSG 67%-33% Aston VillaShots: 6-10Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 0-2Touches in opposition box: 11-17.

After one added minute, the first half is brought to an end and we are all square at 1-1 in Salzburg. Kvaratskhelia had put PSG in front but Madjo’s goal on the stroke of half-time has Aston Villa level at the break.

On the stroke of half-time, the 17-year-old levels for Aston Villa and finally takes his fourth big chance of the night. It is perhaps the hardest chance he has had as McGinn’s cross comes all the way to the back post. Madjo is being held by Pacho but somehow gets his foot to it and his shot goes into the roof of the net. What a moment for the 17-year-old!

Brian Madjo at 17-years-old scores in the UEFA Super Cup Final 🤯📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/PccX7FxjAr.

Madjo has his third massive chance of this first half and this shot comes off the post. Buendia feeds a pass forward into the path of Madjo, who appeared to be blocked by Pacho but he outmuscles him. Madjo then fires towards goal but it strikes the outside of the post. In a parallel universe, Madjo could have ahd a first-half hat-trick.

Aston Villa have had a few great chances in this first half and there is another. A free-kick into the PSG penalty area causes challenges for the French side and Kamara’s header towards goal is saved by Safonov.

It has been revealed that madjo has his second huge chance of this first half. Once more it is McGinn who provides the cross. The Scot does really well on the right side of the box to fake the cross with his left and instead delivers with his right. He picks out Madjo at the back post and the 17-year-old should score but his header misses the target. What a story it would have been had the 17-year-old scored two goals against the Champions League winners.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa have just settled things down. Either side of Kvaratskhelia’s goal, they were on the ropes but have calmed things down.

In a recent development, hemmings is played in and he could potentially have gone down twice under challenges from Hakimi and then Mendes. The ball then falls to 17-year-old Madjo on the left side of the box. He opens up his body and tries to curl into the far corner but his effort goes wide.

According to recent reports, referees are now hot on players taking too long over throw-ins, with Mendes falling foul of that. That is one of the fairly latest rules that will be good for the game.

A huge chance for 17-year-old Madjo to equalise. McGinn picks out the young striker with a sublime cross from the right. Madjo is just eight yards out and has a free header but it goes just wide of the far post. Aston Villa should be level.

Brian Madjo with a significant chance to put Aston Villa level 😮📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/pqsC5Hor15.

In a recent development, after Aston Villa had made a solid start to this game, it is all PSG right now and Villa are on the ropes at the moment. PSG work it beautifully down their left after a sublime one-two between Mendes and Kvaratskhelia. Mendes drives down the left wing and has a cross into the box first-time which he declines. The Portuguese defender then has four different teammates that he could pick out in the penalty area but his cross misses all four.

Sources indicate that PSG want a penalty. Kvaratskhelia shows great feet out on the left to drive into the Aston Villa penalty area. Gomes is on his back and Kvaratskhelia goes down. It did look like he was always looking to go down and it would have been very soft.

A few minutes after I mentioned that Aston Villa had done a decent job of keeping PSG at bay, Luis Enrique’s side take the lead. Bizot had just made a great reflex save to deny Doue but he is unable to stop Kvaratskhelia’s effort. The Georgian cuts inside onto his right just inside the Aston Villa penalty area and gets his shot away rapidly after quick feet. There is great venom on the shot and it beats Bizot, who thought Kvaratskhelia was going to go for the far corner but instead hit it at the near post. Could Bizot have saved that? Perhaps but Kvaratskhelia did belt that shot.

Khvicha Kvaratskhelia puts PSG 1-0 ahead vs Aston Villa 🔥📺 TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/BIf8njpaSx.

As you would expect, PSG are dominating possession but thus far have been unable to create any genuine chances, much to Aston Villa’s credit. But, with the players PSG have at their disposal, they can cause chaos in a moment.

Tensions just start to simmer. McGinn gives a foul away on Mendes, who then attempts to take the free-kick a good few yards further forward from where it was. McGinn repeatedly tries to stop Mendes from taking it further forward before the referee steps in to end the dispute.

Recent findings suggest that moments later, Kamara decides to shoot from range and his low, driving effort goes wide of Safonov’s right post. With Onana injured long-term and Tielemans now at Manchester United, Kamara’s importance to Aston Villa is even higher.

Sources indicate that in last year’s Super Cup, PSG were stunned in the first hour against Tottenham as went 2-0 down before coming back to win on penalties. PSG have played fewer friendlies than Aston Villa up until this point so there may be a little more rustiness in Luis Enrique’s side than Unai Emery’s.

It has been revealed that this is going to be a very tall order for Aston Villa, who look very different tonight to how they ended last season, up against a team of PSG’s calibre. Not only have Villa sold some key players like Rogers and Tielemans but the likes of Konsa and Watkins are yet to return after the World Cup.

McGinn is afforded too much space and time to cut onto his left foot out on the right and whip a dangerous cross towards the far post. Pacho is on hand to head away with a great defensive header.

Recent findings suggest that moments later, good work from Maatsen out on the left earns Aston Villa a corner. Unai Emery’s side have made a decent start to this game. Buendia’s delivery into the near post is headed away by Marquinhos.

We are under way in Salzburg, where it has been a very hot day but the temperature has cooled a touch with the sun having set in Austria.

Some huge banners are on display on the pitch, displaying not only the emblems of the two clubs but also images of the trophy lifts that have earned these sides a place in tonight’s game. Both sides emerge from the tunnel, past the trophies they won with the two captains carrying them out, and we are moments away from kick-off in Salzburg. PSG forwards Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool this summer and both are on the bench for PSG tonight. As PSG close in on moves for Ferran Torres and Mika Godts, could Liverpool’s moves for Barcola and Mbaye accelerate in the next few days? Barcola has only recently returned to training after the World Cup and is joined on the bench by compatriot Ousmane Dembele. Sources indicate that “There is a lot of change but when you look at other clubs in England, there is a lot of change. According to recent reports, what will we learn from the “fresh Aston Villa” tonight? After the sales of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, this is a Villa team in transition.

Unai Emery virtually admitted last night it could be another slow start to the season, like last year. Villa face a full-strength PSG team hoping to win the Super Cup for the second time in a row.

I don’t think we can take much from this result tonight, whatever it is. Villa cannot be properly judged until the window closes. Don’t bother telling that to Unai Emery, though. He is ready to continue defying the doubters.

Sources indicate that the Champions League and Europa League winners fight it out in the Uefa Super Cup in Salzburg as PSG take on Aston Villa. PSG took on English opposition in the Super Cup a year ago, when they played Tottenham. PSG fell 2-0 down in that game in Udine but scored two late goals to take it to penalties, where they won 4-3. These sides met in the Champions League knockout stages two seasons ago; PSG did progress from the quarter-final encounter as they went on to win the competition but not without a scare as Aston Villa did win at Villa Park and PSG only progressed 5-4 on aggregate. The two clubs have been involved in a transfer this week, with left-back Lucas Digne re-joining PSG from Aston Villa.

Sources indicate that aston Villa have played in the Super Cup once before back in 1982 when they took in Barcelona. They lost the first leg 1-0 over at Camp Nou but fought back to win the second leg 3-0 at Villa Park to claim the trophy. Aston Villa were last in action out in the Far East last Friday, falling to a 2-1 defeat to Bayern Munich in Hong Kong. It has been a substantial summer of change at the club, with key starters like Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans departing and the likes of Alejandro Garnacho and Joao Gomes arriving.

In a recent development, “I feel like the club is in a new era, with this possibility to fight for trophies,” Unai Emery told Uefa. “We are trying to be successful through, firstly, [building] a winning team, and then aiming for the positive consequences after it; winning trophies. To play the UEFA Super Cup is another opportunity to be there, the opportunity to win a trophy, to play against Paris Saint-Germain; the [best] team in the world now and another team we can compare [ourselves] with.”.

Emery has confirmed that Ezri Konsa, Ollie Watkins and Emiliano Martinez will not be involved as they are still on their breaks following the World Cup.

PSG have now won back-to-back Champions Leagues, beating Arsenal in the final last season. They have only played a couple of friendlies in pre-season, losing 3-0 to Mallorca before drawing 1-1 against Manchester United. Luis Enrique’s side will take on Lens in the Trophée des Champions on Sunday before kicking off the defence of their Ligue 1 title at home to Rennes.

“I focus on renewing that desire to win again,” Enrique told Uefa. “It is difficult to keep winning. Right now, we have a unique challenge; something that is practically unprecedented in the history of European football, which is to draw level with Real Madrid if we can win a third consecutive Champions League. No-one in history has won three in a row, only Real Madrid. We can equal them. But I do not think there is any team in Europe more motivated than us.

It has been revealed that “No-one rules out PSG any more. Two years ago, it was impossible to put us among the favourites; not impossible, but we were not one of the favourites. Now, no one would say that Paris Saint-Germain are not the favourites. That is something we have earned, but if we are going to maintain that position, we have to work even harder.”.

PSG have added Monaco winger Maghnes Akliouche and Digne to their ranks this summer. They are also pushing to sign Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Mika Godts from Ajax. Bradley Barcola and Ibrahim Mbaye have both been linked with moves to Liverpool but have been included in their squad for tonight’s game, as have Akliouche and Digne.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Seagulls looked on course for at least a point at the MKM Stadium, before two stoppage-time goals from Oli McBurnie condemned them to defeat.

Hurzeler – who was booked by the referee late on in the match – felt Brighton had been the better side for much of the contest. But he criticised their performance after the opening 65 minutes, admitting they had allowed Hull back into the game.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Speaking to Match of the Day, he remarked: "For 65 minutes we showed a good performance then we chopped our intensity, levels and standards.

Industry observers note that "In the Premier League they can punish you especially after a red card. Overall a frustrating afternoon, a frustrating game but we have to keep going.".

Brighton were reduced to ten men in the 89th minute, when Costinha received a second yellow card for pushing Sorba Thomas to the ground.

McBurnie then struck in the 92nd and 95th minutes to secure all three points for Hull.

Asked whether the dismissal had contributed to the late goals, Hurzeler said: "Of course when you are one man down, the red card plays a role.".

The Brighton boss also acknowledged the outstanding performance of Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis, who made several crucial saves to keep his side in the game.

Recent findings suggest that "We have to give credit to him. He made a good performance but in the end it's our responsibility," Hurzeler stated.

Speaking to Sky Sports, Hurzeler described Hull's opening goal as a ‘lucky punch’ but insisted Brighton had to take responsibility for the result.

Recent findings suggest that "That's football. The Premier League is ruthless. Hull scored with a lucky punch, we have to accept it and be better next time.”.

He suggested his players had become impatient as they struggled to make their chances count.

"We rushed things, we lost a bit of intensity, we tried to force things because we weren't patient enough," he mentioned.

"For 65 minutes we could easily win the game.

"You can easily get frustrated if you miss so many chances.".

Hurzeler was also full of praise for Tzolakis, describing him as a ‘great goalkeeper’ who had produced a ‘big performance’.

The Brighton manager was asked about a penalty appeal involving Pascal Gross but said he had not watched the incident back.

"I didn't see it back,” he added.

"The referee wasn't the reason why we lost today.”.

Hurzeler insisted his team would analyse what went wrong but stressed the importance of maintaining their standards in the Premier League.

"We will analyse it – that's the process we follow," he told Match of the Day.

It has been revealed that "I always emphasize keep staying humble. We have to outwork the opponent otherwise the opponents are too good in the Premier League and that's what we have to do better next time.".

Published: 10:42 EST, 17 November 2026 | Updated: 12:38 EST, 17 November 2026.

Gary Neville has stood up for under-fire Manchester United man Diogo Dalot – and named three of his defensive team-mates he would rather see leave the club before him.

The Portugal international's limp performances have come under heavy scrutiny this season with the decline of Michael Carrick's side as autumn has worn on.

But as Mauricio Pochettino prepares to take over at Old Trafford, Neville urged the new manager not to immediately expel the defender, despite his drop-off in form.

Recent findings suggest that 'I think if he was in a decent back four he'd be alright,' Neville told Stick to United co-host Mark Goldbridge on Tuesday. 'But he's got a shocking back four alongside him.

Recent findings suggest that 'Positionally he's not great. He could be better on the ball. He could be better at everything he does. Of course he could. I just think he's such an easy target, Dalot. I honestly do.'.

Neville admitted that sometimes he listens to his fellow Man United-supporting friends deriding Dalot and wonders 'are they watching something that I don't see?'.

Gary Neville has defended Man United star Diogo Dalot - arguing that he has team-mates who are far weaker.

The Portugal international has come in for heavy criticism from supporters this season.

But in his opinion, there are three defenders that he would let go in the 'first wave' of changes in Manchester.

Sources indicate that 'I'd be getting (Noussair) Mazraoui well gone before him,' he continued. 'I'd be getting (Lisandro) Martinez gone well before him. I'll be getting (Matthijs) De Ligt gone well before him.

Industry observers note that '(De Ligt has) got one major problem. He doesn’t play football. If a player is injury prone and doesn't play football, just because he hasn't played doesn't mean to say that he should go above a player who's played every single week and he's throwing his hand up. You want someone who's actually reliable and play. De Ligt has to go. De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui.'.

Another stalwart in the team that Neville was keen to have a second chance under Pochettino was Luke Shaw.

According to recent reports, 'He will keep Shaw because he knows him and he'll probably get the best out of him. The problem with Luke is injuries,' he added. 'So he'll have to manage him. So he'll have to bring a left back in. But let's just say who he'll keep.

Industry observers note that 'He'll keep Shaw. He'll keep (Harry) Maguire because he'll trust him and he'll think that he's basically a soldier and someone who can do a job for him.

'He'll keep (Leny) Yoro because I think he'll think "I've got something there that I can work with". (But) I think he's a little bit gangly, all over the place right now. And he looks like he's going to slip every time. He's got that sort of Bambi-on-ice (look).

Recent findings suggest that 'Physically what will happen is with Yoro, he'll go one way or the other. I like the fact he's been brought into the French team. It tells me sometimes you just have got to connect the dots and think, "okay, well, if they think he's good, then we must be missing something here because we're not seeing it yet, are we?".'.

Neville went on to suggest that Yoro was lacking the connection within his body that Premier League rivals such as Jeremy Jacquet are already able to harness – something Sir Alex Ferguson had identified in Rio Ferdinand when he was at West Ham.

Like Ferdinand, Neville backed Yoro to flourish as he taps into that connection and improves his strength and stability.

Sources indicate that 'So Yoro he will keep: Yoro, Maguire and Shaw I think he'll keep and I think he'll keep Dalot. To start with,' Neville said. 'He'll have to bring in three defenders to go above them. Let's be clear. He'll have to bring in three defenders.

Industry observers note that 'Mazraoui I would lose, De Ligt I would lose because he's injury prone. Martinez 100 per cent. 100 per cent. 100 per cent.'.

As well as struggling for form this season, Martinez has been a challenging presence in the Man United squad this term, boldly calling out the Man United hierarchy during a firebrand interview last month.

Neville was more interested in new head coach Mauricio Pochettino despatching Noussair Mazraoui and Matthijs de Ligt.

Lisandro Martinez has been an unsettled presence in the side this season and hit out at the club's recruiting last month.

The Argentina star implied that he was disappointed with the club's recruitment strategy over the summer, and was forced to hold clear-the-air talks to smooth his return to the side.

Neville added that he would send Ayden Heaven on loan to get experience in the lower divisions to 'build' his ability up, as it was borderline 'unfair' to be 'putting him in' the side at present.

But not all of the changes can come swiftly for Pochettino, who has little time before taking charge of Man United against Liverpool at Anfield this weekend.

In a recent development, 'First wave, end of the season,' Neville clarified of what he believes Pochettino's plan for change will be. 'No, he can't get rid of (them all) in January.

Industry observers note that 'He has to bring one or two defenders in January if he can. But he can't get rid of all those in his first wave. He's only got one month till January.'.

The drawn-out process of sacking Carrick began last week when Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada flew to Monaco for talks with co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer ownership group.

While his future was on the chopping block, Carrick held training sessions at Carrington before the axe finally swung last Thursday.

Pochettino was appointed days later and gave a tearful farewell press conference ahead of his penultimate game with the United States national team on Saturday.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he told the press. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

Sources indicate that ‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay. I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

Industry observers note that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

By Seye Omidiora | 21 Nov 2026 19:35.

Manchester City will welcome a return to the Champions League on Tuesday as they host Napoli at the Etihad Stadium on matchday five.

Enzo Maresca's men have claimed nine points from a possible 12 in Europe, a record that is evidently superior to their domestic form, which has seen them fail to win in four matches, losing three during that period.

The Citizens, though, sit seventh in the Champions League, inside the coveted top-eight positions at the halfway point of the league phase, and are chasing a third consecutive success in the competition and their fourth overall.

Here, Sports Mole rounds up Man City's latest injury and suspension news ahead of their clash against Napoli, who lie 27th in the 36-team league phase with three points.

Sources indicate that possible return date: December 19 (vs. Hull City).

Antonine Semenyo is still sidelined with the knee injury sustained against Ipswich Town on October 17, likely keeping him out until just before Christmas, barring any setbacks.

Possible return date: November 24 (vs. Napoli).

Matheus Nunes missed Portugal's fixtures during the international break due to an unspecified concern that also prevented him from featuring in Saturday's 1-1 draw with Fulham.

However, the versatile player could return against Napoli after undergoing the necessary pre-match checks.

Man City have no suspended players for this match.

Selfie-seekers bring Man Utd vs Leeds match to premature end

📅 13 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 20 min read (4092 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~20 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events?
  • There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.
  • Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, aren’t friendlies supposed to be non-events? Manchester United against Leeds United in Dublin always had the capacity to be lively, but try explaining the half hour that Bruno Fernandes experienced in one breath. It would be impossible.

There was only one player the vast majority of the crowd wanted to see in the grandiosely named Boyle Sports Cup and, in chronological order from his 60th minute introduction, he received a standing ovation, hit the bar, had a goal disallowed, missed a penalty in a shoot-out and lifted a trophy.

Most remarkably – and, certainly, worryingly – of all, he was central to the game being ended early as five young boys, one after the other, breached security and ran to him in the middle of pitch, all of them successfully posing for photos with the Portuguese.

You could say it was harmless fun but it should not have happened and the flummoxed faces that were pulled on the Manchester United bench, as an army in high-visibility jackets stood and watched it all unfold, suggested they took a dim view.

Sources indicate that it was a shame because in that cameo, Fernandes showed he has returned from the World Cup in excellent shape, the tempo of United’s play immediately lifting when he had the ball. It is wrong to make conclusions in the summer, but you are on safe ground to state he will be integral to their ambitions.

Croke Park is a stadium steeped in history and another chapter was penned here, as the capacity crowd made this the highest attended soccer match in Ireland with 82,000 coming through the gates: it is a magnificent venue, one that would be well capable of hosting a Champions League final.

Michael Carrick hopes in years to come that is the stage where his team will be but, right now, it is a case of learning to walk again before they can run and he more than anyone will know how far off that target is, not that it will stop him trying to get there.

The one thing that is obvious about the way United play under him is the first thought from everyone is to go forward promptly. Yes, this was only a friendly, but the ambition to be on the front foot and cause problems was evident from the start.

The team in red had much the better of the opening exchanges, with Diogo Dalot having the first shot that went over but, unlike on July 25, when Mayo beat Kerry here in Gaelic football’s All Ireland final, which went viral, nobody was cheering the sight of a ball clearing the bar.

It was like a home game for United and the majority got what they wanted in the 15th minute when a slick counter-attack ended with Bryan Mbuemo sliding a pass into Joshua Zikzee, who rifled past James Trafford with a first-time finish.

Devastating counterattack! 💥Manchester United break and Joshua Zirkzee is there to finish it off 🤩 pic.twitter.com/y6QHbZMi7n.

Zirkzee is unlikely to be part of Carrick’s squad beyond the transfer window, with interest from clubs in Italy, and it would be disingenuous to suggest his career at Old Trafford has been successful, but his attitude was exemplary and he played as if he was desperate to change his manager’s mind.

There may have been an anticipation that United would stride clear, but this game was also about Leeds, whose summer has been encouraging and whose confidence from staying up last season has evidently enabled them to blossom.

It has been revealed that you would be way off the mark if you include them in your conversations about which clubs are going to be relegated next May, and the sense they showed to stay with Daniel Farke has paid off. They have bought some good players, not least goalkeeper James Trafford and Harry Wilson.

Top stop from James Trafford! 🚫The Leeds United keeper has been busy in the first half... pic.twitter.com/VKmxNVKBsA.

Trafford has done the right thing getting away from Manchester City and you could argue that he is already reaping the benefit of playing for a manager who wants him, as he made a fabulous save in the 23rd minute to thwart Mbuemo. It was all part of performance that led to him being named player of the match.

He was involved in the move that brought the Leeds equaliser, too, as his long clearance caused uncertainty and led to Tyler Fletcher being pickpocketed by Dan James and he nudged a pass into Brenden Aaronson, who kept his cool and danced into the area, ignoring Senne Lammens, to finish.

Leeds hit back with their first shot on target! 💥Brenden Aaronson with a cool finish 🥶 pic.twitter.com/5WsSZY41j6.

It was an entertaining affair, mercifully lacking the bile that would usually bubble away when it is staged in England, and the longer the game advanced, the better Leeds looked. They finished the opening period strongly and came back after the restart, with 10 changes, in the same fettle.

Farke, whose team had shown their ability to score heavily when they pummelled Liverpool 4-2 in Chicago 10 days ago, would have taken plenty of encouragement, but the perfectionist in him would have cursed the opportunities that were squandered early in the second period.

In a recent development, the misses proved costly as the game meandered and the shoot-out went United’s way, after Wilson and James Justin failed from 12 yards, with Noussair Mazraoui thumping in the decisive kick. It really is never dull.

Manchester United Lammens (Mee 61); Dalot (Mazraoui 60), Yoro, Heaven (Armer 46), Amass (Shaw 60); Santos (Collyer 46), T Fletcher (Tielemans 61); Diallo (J Fletcher 60), Zirkzee (Cunha 60), Dorgu (Thompson 46); Mbuemo (Fernandes 60).Subs not used Heath, Honor, Lacey, Gabriel.

Leeds United Trafford (Cairns 46); Bijol (Rodon 46), Muharemovic (Cresswell 46), Bornauw; Bogle (Gnonto 46), Longstaff (Stach 46), Tanaka (Ampadu 46), Chadwick (Justin 46); James (Okafor 46), Aaronson (Wilson 46); Nmecha (Calvert-Lewin 46).Subs not used Mahady, Lienou, Mills, Piroe.

It has been revealed that decent enough watch for roughly half the game, settled on a shoot-out in which Alex Cairns got nowhere near any of Manchester United’s penalties. Doubt he will lose much sleep over it. Bruno Fernandes grinned broadly when he missed.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 5.

According to recent reports, bottom left. Manchester United win the Boyle Sports Cup.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 4.

Leeds United 4 Manchester United 3.

According to recent reports, top right. Sudden death now effectively.

Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

Rolls it casually past the right post.

Leeds United 3 Manchester United 3.

Leeds United 2 Manchester United 3.

Leeds United 2 Manchester United 2.

Leeds United 1 Manchester United 2.

Bottom right. Took it very quickly.

Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

Leeds United 1 Manchester United 1.

Smacks it even higher into the top right.

Leeds United 1 Manchester United 0.

So there will be another short delay.

And I think Amapdu’s signal means Leeds will go first.

The ref decides to call time as the stewards cannot catch the juvenile intruders.

Not sure what we can say about stadium safety here but the game has ended prematurely after five kids came on, all of whom got to Bruno Fernandes to take selfies. It was very funny but, equally, plenty on the Manchester United bench were far from happy. Penalties to follow.

Some sealion ball juggling from Mazraoui involving foot, thigh and head, gets him past Justin on the right  but Gnonto heads away his cross.

According to recent reports, two young Man Utd fans run on to the pitch to try to take selfies with Man utd players. They are joined by three more and now another.

It’s like Euro 2016 all over again.

Bruno Fernandes lets fly from 20 yards, cushioning a pass from Tielemans before hammering his shot into the crossbar with little backlift.

Gnonto breaks down the right, plays it infield to Wilson who runs at the heart of the Man Utd defence but smacks his shot into a defender.

There will be a shootout if the match is drawn after 90 minutes. The Boyle Sports Cup cannot be shared, it seems.

Seven Manchester United changes: Mee, Tielmans, Shaw, Bruno Fernandes, Jack Fletcher, Matheus Cunha and Mazraoui incoming for Dalot, Lammens, Amass, Mbeumo, Diallo, Zirkzee and Tyler Fletcher.

In a recent development, good evening and welcome to live coverage of the pre-season friendly between Manchester United and Leeds United at a sold-out Croke Park in Dublin. Last year Leeds played Milan in the Irish capital and drew a crowd of 52,000 but at the GAA citadel, as I think I’m contractually obliged to call it, there will be 83,000 present, a testament to the Premier League’s reach and these two clubs’ popularity in Ireland founded on the exploits of Billy Whelan, Noel Cantwell, Johnny Giles, Roy Keane, Gary Kelly et al. It’s the first club match ever held at the stadium.

In a recent development, it’s a fixture that always stirs the blood and whenever it comes around you can guarantee that there will be reams of stuff about the War of the Roses, clash in styles, Busby and Revie, Bobby and Jack, large swathes of which this author has been guilty of producing. I’ll spare you all that today because while it’s relevant to fans of both clubs, they know it backwards. And it’s a match that has come around a wee bit too frequently in pre-season recently, first in Perth, Western Australia, in 2019 when Ole Gunnar Solskjaer’s side beat Marcelo Bielsa’s 4-0, then in 2023 in Oslo when Erik ten Haag’s second or third string defeated Daniel Farke’s threadbare, just relegated squad 2-0 and last year in Stockholm, which ended in a 0-0 draw between two scratch sides.

This one comes round later in the pre-season schedule than those three so we can expect to see stronger XIs, at least for part of the game. Leeds’ pre-season has gone well: after a 3-2 defeat by Wrexham in Tampa, they have beaten Sunderland in Fresh Jersey, Liverpool in Chicago and RB Leipzig at Elland Road. Manchester United also lost to Wrexham (in Helsinki) then beat Rosenborg in Trondheim, Atlético in Stockholm and drew one apiece with the European champions, PSG, in Gothenburg last time out.

While Leeds will have latest signing James Trafford available and Noah Okafor, who scored twice in Leeds’ first league victory at Old Trafford for 45 years last April, in the squad for the first time after the World Cup, Manchester United have Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford back in training since the start of the week but it seems too soon for them to start but Youri Tielemans is pushing to make his first start.

Latest Update: ‘They had faith’ – Moyes reflects on Everton legacy ahead of milestone match
